citation.authors: Liu X, Hill AM, West SG, et al.
citation.title: Acute Peanut Consumption Alters Postprandial Lipids and Vascular Responses in Healthy Overweight or Obese Men

population.description: 15 generally healthy overweight or obese men (Methods, Participants: enrolled at BMI 28 to 39 and aged 20 to 65 y, free of diabetes, CVD and other metabolic disease; Results: 40% overweight, 60% obese). Screening was by fasting glucose below 99 mg/dL, fasting TG, LDL, blood pressure and history, not by an oral glucose test, so the group is unselected. Age 26.7 +/- 1.6 and BMI 31.4 +/- 0.8 are printed as means +/- SEM (Table 2, n = 15); sd is SEM x sqrt(15) = 6.197 and 3.098, computed here. Min and max are not printed.

protocols.name: control_shake
protocols.description: Control shake of 1229 kcal (Table 1: 24.8% carbohydrate, 64.7% fat, 8.4% protein, 8.2 g fiber; shake of 34.8 g glucose, 150 g heavy whipping cream, 39 g chocolate syrup, 20 g sunflower oil, 17 g safflower oil, 27 g powdered egg white, 9.6 g fiber supplement), consumed within 15 min after the fasting (10-12 h) baseline sample at minute 0; liquid (a shake). Grams from the printed energy and percentages: carbohydrate 1229 x 0.248 / 4 = 76.2 g, less the printed 8.2 g fiber = 68.0 g (the paper names no diet software and does not say whether its carbohydrate % includes fiber; taken as total carbohydrate, as on US labels, so the README's subtraction applies); fat 1229 x 0.647 / 9 = 88.4 g; protein 1229 x 0.084 / 4 = 25.8 g. Start hour 8.0 is not printed. Prefast 11 h is the midpoint of the printed 10-12 h fast (the README has no rule for a printed range). Samples at 0, 30, 60, 120 and 240 min. Serum glucose and insulin (Quest Diagnostics Chem 24 panel on serum), n = 15.

meals.food: shake: glucose, whipping cream, chocolate syrup, oils, egg white

protocols.name: peanut_shake
protocols.description: Peanut shake of 1198 kcal (Table 1 and Methods: 25.9% carbohydrate, 66.2% fat, 8.5% protein, 8.2 g fiber; 34.8 g glucose, 137 g heavy whipping cream, 39 g chocolate syrup and 85 g (3.0 ounces) ground peanuts with skins), consumed within 15 min after the fasting (10-12 h) baseline sample at minute 0; liquid (a shake). The abstract prints 40.0% carbohydrate, 47.7% fat, 13.2% protein for this shake; Table 1, the Methods sentence on the shake and the paper's statement that the shakes were matched for carbohydrate and saturated fat with the control (control 24.8% of 1229 kcal) agree with each other and not with the abstract, so Table 1 is used. Grams: carbohydrate 1198 x 0.259 / 4 = 77.6 g, less the printed 8.2 g fiber = 69.4 g (same fiber assumption as the control arm); fat 1198 x 0.662 / 9 = 88.1 g; protein 1198 x 0.085 / 4 = 25.5 g. Start hour 8.0 is not printed. Prefast 11 h is the midpoint of the printed 10-12 h fast. Samples at 0, 30, 60, 120 and 240 min. Serum glucose and insulin, n = 15.
